fixed_findings: Output confinement originally checked direct argv only; final code confines output to the observer observations directory and checks recursively pinned nested invocation paths.
Exceptions after child creation could leave the child running; final code checks waitability, terminates/reaps the owned child session with escalation and records incomplete observation.
reviewed_behavior: Dry-run is default; execution requires explicit --execute.
The pinned audit argv is used without a shell or cwd/environment/stdio overrides. The distinct child session is explicitly disclosed and supports owned signal forwarding.
Exact invocation and nested invocation hashes, runner hash and observer hash are recorded, with after-execution equality booleans.
Output directories and files are new and cannot overwrite prior evidence; candidate/build/audit output paths are excluded.
Normal child exit codes and signal-derived shell status are retained. Observation success is distinct from child/audit success.

Linux wait4 produces raw accounting for the waited outer audit process and accounted descendants. The report explicitly avoids interpreting largest-process high-water as simultaneous process-tree RSS or per-Lean attribution.
limits: Resource observations do not weaken or replace source, build, exact-type, axiom, broad or fresh-kernel acceptance gates.
Observer failure, SIGKILL or host failure may leave incomplete evidence, which is never proof acceptance.
Existing freeze semantics require no noncooperating transient writers.
